name: Morann

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Morann was an Irish hero. Several medieval sources describe him as a wise brehon, or judge. He wore a chain around his neck. If he began to speak false words or give an unjust sentence, the chain tightened until it strangled him. He could also place the chain on the neck of a person on trial. It worked the same way there, tightening until it strangled the accused, if that one lied. The chain made plain the truth of every speech and every judgment.
objective: Document the Irish hero and brehon Morann and his truth chain.
key_results: Record Morann as a wise brehon or judge of medieval Irish sources.
Record the chain that strangled him for false words or unjust sentences.
Record the chain that strangled an accused person who lied.
